title: Scholar Rock Wins FDA Approval for First SMA Muscle Loss Treatment
summary: Scholar Rock received FDA approval for Isembyld, the first therapy targeting muscle loss in spinal muscular atrophy for patients ages 2 and older already on SMN2-targeting drugs. Clinical trial data showed Isembyld combined with SMN2-targeting therapy improved motor skills in young patients after on
takeaways: Isembyld approved for SMA patients age 2+ currently on SMN2-targeting therapies
First drug targeting muscle loss in SMA after decades of failed myostatin inhibition efforts
Trial showed motor skill improvement vs. decline in placebo group (statistically significant)

title: Scientists discover human heart muscle can regenerate after heart attack
summary: Researchers at Australian institutions demonstrated for the first time that human heart muscle cells can regenerate after a heart attack, challenging decades of assumption that cardiac tissue loss is permanent. takeaways: First demonstration of cardiac regeneration in human heart tissue, not just mice

title: Axons may naturally resemble strings of pearls, overturning century-old textbook depiction
summary: Johns Hopkins researchers discovered that axons naturally feature pearl-like structures (non-synaptic varicosities) rather than smooth tubes as shown in textbooks for over a century. These repeating bulges influence electrical signal transmission and brain cell signaling.
takeaways: Study published Nature Neuroscience, December 2, 2024
Lead researcher: Shigeki Watanabe, Johns Hopkins associate professor
Pearl-like structures documented in mouse neurons and human brain tissue
Non-synaptic varicosities distinct from larger synaptic varicosities at neurotransmitter sites
Structures influence electrical signal travel; part of normal architecture, not damage

title: FDA Approves First Gene Therapy for Sanfilippo Syndrome Type A
summary: The FDA approved Fayuvi, the first gene therapy specifically designed to treat Sanfilippo syndrome type A, an ultra-rare childhood neurodegenerative disease. The approval provides the first medical treatment option for patients previously without intervention.
takeaways: First FDA-approved treatment for Sanfilippo syndrome type A
Developed by Ultragenyx
Targets ultra-rare childhood neurodegenerative disease (childhood Alzheimer's)

title: Scientists identify immune system overreaction as driver of rapid aging
summary: Researchers at Hebrew University discovered that the immune sensor cGAS triggers rapid aging by mistaking damaged DNA for viral threats. Reducing cGAS activity improved tissue health in fast-aging models, challenging assumptions about DNA damage and cellular decline.
takeaways: cGAS immune sensor confuses damaged DNA with viral threats
Activates chronic sterile inflammation damaging healthy tissue
cGAS also disrupts DNA repair when entering cell nucleus
Reducing cGAS activity improved tissue health across biological systems
Research focused on Ataxia-Telangiectasia and Bloom syndrome

title: Scientists reconstruct videos from mouse brain activity
summary: University College London scientists reconstructed 10-second video clips from neural signals in mice's visual cortex using single-cell recordings and a dynamic neural encoding model. The technique reveals how the brain processes and filters visual information differently from physical stimuli.
takeaways: Reconstructed 10-second videos from mouse visual cortex neurons
Used single-cell recordings rather than broader brain imaging
Dynamic neural encoding model predicted individual neuron responses
Method reveals visual features the brain emphasizes or filters
Published in eLife journal

title: Ancient DNA reveals plague killed Siberian hunter-gatherers 5,500 years before Black Death
summary: Ancient DNA analysis reveals Yersinia pestis killed Siberian hunter-gatherers approximately 5,500 years ago, predating the Black Death by millennia. DNA from the plague bacterium was detected in 18 of 46 individuals tested (40 percent), with an unusually high concentration of child and adolescent de
takeaways: Plague detected in prehistoric Lake Baikal remains ~5,500 years ago
40 percent detection rate in 46 individuals tested
Concentrated deaths among children and young teenagers
Published in Nature, led by Ruairidh Macleod (Oxford)
Early strains may have carried severe immune-reaction genetic factors

title: Scientists Identify Major Epigenetic Brain Changes Between Ages 50 and 75
summary: Researchers identified major epigenetic and structural brain changes occurring between ages 50 and 75, including sharp decline in embryonically-derived microglia, reduced blood-brain barrier maintenance, and erosion of three-dimensional genome architecture. takeaways: Age window: ages 50–75 shows sharp decline in embryonically-derived microglia
Microglia replaced by cells with pro-inflammatory molecular signatures
Substantial decline in blood-brain barrier maintenance populations
Broad erosion of 3D genome architecture across multiple brain cell types
Aging is strongest risk factor for Alzheimer's disease

title: Fourth Measles Death Reported in Pennsylvania Within One Month
summary: Pennsylvania reported a fourth measles-related death on September 15, 2026—an unvaccinated 18-year-old who died of acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM). First measles deaths in Pennsylvania in 35 years
U.S. 2026: worst year for measles since 1991; 7 deaths in last two years

title: New World Screwworm Parasite Returns to United States After Eradication
summary: The New World screwworm—a flesh-eating parasite eradicated from the U.S. in the 1950s—has returned with confirmed detections in Texas and New Mexico. takeaways: Parasite eradicated from U.S. in 1950s; returns with detections in Texas and New Mexico
1950s damage estimate: $50–$100 million annually in U.S. livestock losses
New World screwworm feeds on healthy, living flesh (unlike most fly larvae)
Researchers developed tracking dashboard to predict spread and identify county-level risk
Females lay eggs in open wounds or natural body openings

title: Abbott settles for $385 million over closure of largest U.S. baby formula plant
summary: Abbott Laboratories agreed to a $385 million settlement resolving claims tied to contamination investigations at its Sturgis, Michigan baby formula plant, the largest in the U.S., which closed in February 2022 and triggered nationwide supply shortages. Abbott states the settlement involves no admiss
takeaways: $385 million Abbott settlement over Sturgis facility closure
Sturgis plant: largest U.S. baby formula facility
Facility closed February 2022, triggering recalls and supply shortages
Government tests of unopened product negative for Cronobacter sakazakii
Criminal investigation closed by Justice Department

title: Scientists discover 3D DNA organization disruption in Alzheimer's disease
summary: Researchers discovered that Alzheimer's disease disrupts the three-dimensional organization of DNA in brain cells, altering gene expression in ways previously unexplored in the disease. The finding, published in Science, opens new avenues for understanding disease mechanisms beyond amyloid-beta plaq
takeaways: 3D genome folding disrupted in Alzheimer's-affected brain cells
Study examined postmortem prefrontal cortex samples using GAGE-seq technology
Higher-order chromatin alterations identified as component of disease pathology
Research from Carnegie Mellon, University of Pittsburgh, and University of Washington
Affects approximately 7 million Americans

title: Semaglutide shown to slow aging and extend lifespan in mice
summary: Semaglutide, the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy, extended lifespan by nearly 100 days in older mice while improving memory, muscle function, and reducing aging markers, according to an NIH-funded UC Berkeley study. takeaways: Median lifespan extended by nearly 100 days in treated mice

Metabolic rate remained unchanged (unlike calorie restriction)
Suggests separate aging pathway beyond appetite suppression

title: AstraZeneca breast cancer pill fails in pivotal trial
summary: AstraZeneca's camizestrant (Etcamah) failed its pivotal SERENA-4 trial, showing no improvement in progression-free survival compared to standard treatment for advanced ER-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer. The drug had received accelerated FDA approval in early September 2026 for resistant tumor
takeaways: Camizestrant failed SERENA-4 pivotal trial on September 12, 2026

Company continuing early-stage disease testing despite first-line market setback

title: Scientists Identify Method to Breach Pancreatic Cancer's Immune Shield
summary: Researchers at University of Miami's Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center found that blocking IL1RAP, an inflammatory receptor, can disrupt pancreatic tumors' protective immune shield and enhance treatment effectiveness. takeaways: IL1RAP inhibition reduced tumor-protecting immune-suppressive cells and decreased fibrosis

IL1RAP functions as shared control point linking tumor cells, immune cells, and fibroblasts
First-of-its-kind neoadjuvant clinical trial planned with chemoimmunotherapy
Targets pancreatic tumors' paradox: highly inflamed yet immune-suppressive

title: UCLA develops cancer-fighting T cells from cord blood for solid tumors
summary: UCLA researchers engineered T cells from cord blood stem cells that attacked solid tumors in mice while avoiding graft-versus-host disease. takeaways: AlloESO-T cells successfully controlled ovarian cancer and melanoma in mice with single dose
TCR therapy detects internal protein fragments, broader than CAR T-cell approach
Current personalized T-cell therapy costs six figures and takes weeks to produce
Cord blood cells enable pre-manufactured frozen batches for multiple patients
Published in Cell Reports Medicine

title: New experimental drug targets mesothelioma by disabling tumor antioxidant defense

takeaways: Drug controlled disease progression in 67% of relapsed mesothelioma patients

title: Hidden immune organ in skull discovered to fight brain cancer in mice
summary: Researchers at Washington University identified previously unknown immune structures in skull bone marrow that function as rapid-response defense against brain cancer in mice. Evidence of similar immune cells in human skull bone marrow suggests the system may apply broadly, opening new treatment app

title: Natural gut compound from food fermentation shown to repair intestinal lining
summary: University of Louisville researchers identified urolithin A (UroA), a compound produced by gut bacteria when digesting pomegranates, walnuts, and berries, as a potential treatment for inflammatory bowel disease. takeaways: Compound: urolithin A (UroA), produced during digestion of pomegranates, walnuts, berries

Triggers NLRP6 inflammasome to repair gut lining and strengthen barriers

First study showing naturally produced microbial metabolite activates protective mechanisms in intestinal cells

title: Rare genetic mutation dramatically increases lung cancer risk in nonsmokers
summary: Researchers identified a rare genetic mutation that substantially elevates lung cancer risk in nonsmokers, particularly among those born in Southeastern U.S. states.

Biological age assessed using 20 biomarkers

title: Study identifies optimal whole grain intake of 4-6 servings daily for heart health
summary: A meta-analysis of 87 randomized controlled trials found that consuming 4–6 servings of whole grains daily (60–100 grams dry weight) produces the strongest improvements in cardiovascular risk factors including cholesterol, blood pressure, and inflammation.
takeaways: 4–6 servings daily optimal for heart health benefits
60–100 grams per day (dry weight)
Improvements in weight, cholesterol, LDL, triglycerides, blood glucose
Benefits observed at 30–40 grams but plateau at higher levels
Meta-analysis of 87 clinical trials, over 6,500 participants
Published September 15, 2026 in European Heart Journal

title: Scientists create mice with half brains, fill with human organoids, raising ethical questions
summary: Stanford scientists created neuro-chimeric mice with approximately half their brain tissue replaced by human brain organoids, discovering specialized human neurons including those previously found only in large-brain mammals. takeaways: Mice had ~50% brain tissue replaced with human organoids

Large social cognition neurons previously found only in elephants, whales, primates
Published in Nature on September 16, 2026
Raises ethical concerns about human-animal neural hybrids

title: U.S. Records Highest Number of Measles Deaths in Decades
summary: The United States recorded four measles-related deaths in 2026, the highest annual toll since 1992. Pennsylvania reported two additional deaths on September 16, including a 40-year-old woman and 18-year-old, with 693 cases across 38 counties.

title: Discovery of Erucamide Offers New Hope for Retinal Disease Prevention
summary: Scientists at Scripps Research Institute identified erucamide, a naturally occurring molecule in the eye that activates protective immune responses and may slow retinal degeneration. Erucamide levels decline as photoreceptors die, and restoring it stabilized retinal tissue in preclinical models.
takeaways: Erucamide is naturally occurring eye molecule that protects retina
Activates protective immune and cellular responses
Functions as signaling molecule coordinating retinal cells
Published June 19, 2026 in Nature Neuroscience
May lead to treatments for diabetic retinopathy, retinitis pigmentosa, macular degeneration

title: Vera's Trutakna kidney drug shows strong Phase 3 results in IgAN treatment
summary: Vera Therapeutics announced positive final two-year Phase 3 results for Trutakna, demonstrating kidney function stabilization and reduced mortality risk in IgA nephropathy patients. The drug received accelerated FDA approval in July 2026; the company will seek full approval in Q4 2026.
takeaways: Stabilized kidney function in IgAN patients
Reduced kidney-related death and complication risk
Accelerated FDA approval received July 2026

title: Meta-Analysis of 139 Trials Finds Knee Braces Most Effective for Osteoarthritis Pain
summary: A network meta-analysis of 139 clinical trials involving nearly 10,000 patients found knee braces most effective for knee osteoarthritis pain relief, stiffness reduction, and physical function improvement. Water-based therapy proved especially effective for pain; regular exercise provided consistent

title: Definium's LSD therapy eases anxiety in second phase trial
summary: Definium's LSD-based treatment achieved positive anxiety outcomes in a second large clinical trial, advancing psychedelic therapeutics toward regulatory approval.

title: Study of 117-Year-Old Reveals Simultaneous Extreme Aging and Youth
